summary: upload.sh (65 lines, shellcheck clean) passed 41 of 41 checks against a stub gh and a local authenticated git server, using a bundle of main at d855cd6. The final zip carries this log commit on top and is re-run after it; the script itself is byte-identical (sha256 below).

Technique for any script that acts as the user on a third-party host: test it against a policy twin of that host (stub CLI plus a local authenticated git-over-HTTP server) with a decoy stale credential helper, and give every refusal path its own negative control. The decoy run showed plain git is refused with the stale helper while the script's empty-helper reset succeeds, so the harness would have caught a wrong-account push.
